newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace disrupts oil exploration in Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace disrupts oil exploration in Atlantic.

text.p: Two Greenpeace activists on Wednesday frustrated efforts by a survey ship to prospect for oil in the Atlantic Ocean by sitting on its high-powered air guns, the environmental pressure group said.
The move was the latest skirmish in a six-week Greenpeace campaign against seismic surveys of the Atlantic Frontier area to the west of Scotland's Shetland Isles.
The group says the world's existing reserves of hydrocarbons are already so great that they could not all be burned without risking global environmental disaster.
Greenpeace said the two activists, a British woman and an Australian man, climbed on to the guns of the Geo Explorer after it had prepared its testing array to survey part of the seabed.
This stopped the seismic vessel firing the guns, which emit explosions of 225 decibels, one and a half times as loud as a jet aeroplane taking off.

Earlier this week, Greenpeace activists operating from one of the group's ships went into the sea to prevent the Geo Explorer carrying out the task assigned to it by three oil companies, Phillips Petroleum, Enterprise Oil and Agip.

"Today's action is an escalation on the previous use of swimmers in the water, which force the testing vessels to weave in complicated patterns rather than the straight lines required for successful testing," the group said in a statement.
Jon Castle, captain of the Greenpeace vessel, said the surveyors have already lost 52 hours of exploration because of the group's activities.
"Every hour they lose is a gain for the climate," he said.
